Every command of greenlens with its options and examples. The same text is available offline with 'greenlens help &lt;command&gt;'.

## Global options

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | Configuration file. Defaults to /etc/greenlens/greenlens.yaml, then the file of the user |  |
| `--lang` | Language for messages (code: en or es). Defaults to the system locale |  |
| `--no-color` | Do not color the output; NO_COLOR has the same effect |  |
| `-o`, `--output` | Output format (format: table, json, csv or yaml) | `table` |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Print only the result, without progress or advice |  |
| `--raw` | Show values in base units (J, W, g) with full precision |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Print details of every step, such as sensor read errors |  |

## greenlens agent

Run the agent in the foreground: it samples the energy sources, stores the measurements and serves the other commands through its local socket. Under systemd it runs as the greenlens service. SIGHUP reloads the configuration and SIGTERM stops it.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens agent [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens agent
greenlens agent --config /etc/greenlens/greenlens.yaml
```

## greenlens backup

Write a consistent copy of the database to a new file, using the backup interface of SQLite. When the agent is running it makes the copy, so measurements continue and no permissions on its data directory are needed; otherwise the database of this user is copied. The copy is checked before it gets its name, and an existing file is never replaced.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens backup <file> [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--database` | Copy this database file instead of asking the agent |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens backup greenlens-2026-10-20.db
greenlens backup --database /var/lib/greenlens/greenlens.db /srv/backups/greenlens.db
```

## greenlens bench

Send the same prompts to a backend several times, with greedy decoding and a fixed seed, and measure the energy of each run. It reports the energy per generated token with its mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation and 95% confidence interval, and the conditions of the machine. Only the SHA-256 of the prompts is stored, never the prompts. The energy of a run is that attributed to the processes of the backend, so other processes do not change it, and with a calibration only the energy above idle counts.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens bench [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--endpoint` | Base URL of the backend; empty uses the default port of its kind |  |
| `--interval` | Sampling interval of the energy, from 50ms to 10s | `100ms` |
| `--kind` | Kind of backend: ollama, llamacpp, vllm, tgi, sglang, localai or openai | `ollama` |
| `--max-tokens` | Most tokens generated per prompt | `128` |
| `--min-run` | Shortest run; each run repeats the prompts as many times as needed | `1m0s` |
| `--model` | Model to benchmark, as the backend names it |  |
| `--no-save` | Do not store the result in the agent |  |
| `--prompts` | File with one prompt per line instead of the built-in set |  |
| `--runs` | Measured runs, from 2 to 100 | `5` |
| `--warmup` | How long to send prompts before measuring, so the model is loaded and the hardware warm | `30s` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens bench --model qwen2.5:0.5b
greenlens bench --kind llamacpp --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8080 --model q.gguf --runs 10
```

## greenlens calibrate

Measure the power of every domain while the machine is idle and store the median as the idle baseline. The dynamic idle policy subtracts this baseline before attributing energy to processes. Stop other workloads first.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens calibrate [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--duration` | How long to measure | `1m0s` |
| `--interval` | Sampling interval (default: agent.sample_interval) |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens calibrate
greenlens calibrate --duration 5m
```

## greenlens compare

Compare two benchmarks, by their ids, or two models, as backend/model or as a model name, by the energy per generated token measured in a period. It projects the energy, emissions and cost saved if the work of the first were done by the second: 1,000 generated tokens for benchmarks, the tokens the first model generated in the period for models.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens compare <a> <b> [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--from` | Start of the period | `7d` |
| `--to` | End of the period | `now` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens compare 3 7
greenlens compare ollama-11434/llama3.2 ollama-11434/qwen2.5:0.5b --from 7d
```

## greenlens completion

Print the completion script of greenlens for bash, zsh or fish. Save it where the shell loads completions, as in the examples, and open a new shell. Packages install it for you.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens completion bash|zsh|fish [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/greenlens
greenlens completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_greenlens"
greenlens completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/greenlens.fish
```

## greenlens export

Export stored measurements for other tools: node energy per channel, usage per backend, model or consumer, and benchmarks. The output is CSV unless --output json or yaml is given; columns and fields keep the same names in every language, and values are in base units.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens export [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|

## greenlens export benchmarks

Export the stored benchmarks, newest first, with their energy per generated token, standard deviation, coefficient of variation and 95% confidence interval. The JSON output keeps every run.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens export benchmarks [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | Most benchmarks to export, up to 1000 | `1000` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens export benchmarks > benchmarks.csv
greenlens export benchmarks --limit 10 --output json
```

## greenlens export energy

Export the energy of every measured channel in buckets of the period, with its source, domain, quality and number of samples, in joules.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens export energy [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket` | Size of each bucket, such as 1m, 1h or 24h, or none for one total | `1h` |
| `--from` | Start of the period | `24h` |
| `--to` | End of the period | `now` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens export energy --from 7d > energy.csv
greenlens export energy --from 2026-10-01 --to 2026-11-01 --bucket 1m --output json
```

## greenlens export usage

Export the energy attributed to each backend, model or consumer, with its tokens and requests, as one total for the period or one row per bucket.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens export usage [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket` | Size of each bucket, such as 1m, 1h or 24h, or none for one total | `none` |
| `--from` | Start of the period | `24h` |
| `--group` | Group by backend, model or consumer | `model` |
| `--to` | End of the period | `now` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens export usage --from 30d --group consumer > consumers.csv
greenlens export usage --from 7d --bucket 24h --group model --output json
```

## greenlens gui

Ask the running agent for a one-time sign-in link and open it in the default browser with xdg-open. The link works once, within 2 minutes, and signs the browser in with the chosen role.  Over SSH, or without a graphical session, the link is printed instead, with the command that forwards the port of the agent to your computer.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens gui [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--print` | Print the link instead of opening the browser |  |
| `--role` | Role of the session: viewer, operator or admin | `admin` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens gui
greenlens gui --print --role viewer
```

## greenlens license

Show the license of GreenLens, where to get the source code of this version and the third-party components it includes. Use --full for the complete license text and --third-party for the license of every component.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens license [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--full` | Print the complete text of the license |  |
| `--third-party` | Print the license of every third-party component |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens license
greenlens license --full | less
greenlens license --third-party > notices.md
```

## greenlens measure

Measure the energy used while a command runs, while a process and its children run, or while a systemd unit runs, and attribute to it the share of CPU and memory energy that matches its CPU time. With a command, its exit code becomes the exit code of measure and the report goes to standard error.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens measure [-- command] [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--duration` | Stop after this time; by default, when the target ends |  |
| `--interval` | Sampling interval (default: agent.sample_interval) |  |
| `--pid` | Measure this process and its children |  |
| `--report` | Write the report to this file instead of the terminal |  |
| `--unit` | Measure this systemd unit |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens measure -- ollama run llama3.2 "Why is the sky blue?"
greenlens measure --pid 4242 --duration 5m
greenlens measure --unit ollama.service --duration 10m
```

## greenlens proxy

Show the address, upstream and requests of the reverse proxy the agent runs for servers that do not count tokens, such as Ollama. The proxy forwards requests unchanged and reads only token counts; enable it under proxy in the configuration.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens proxy [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens proxy
greenlens report --from 24h --group consumer
```

## greenlens report

Report the energy measured by the agent in a period, by domain and in total, with its emissions and, when a tariff is configured, its cost. With --group, report the energy attributed to each backend or model instead, with its tokens. With --regressions, list the days whose energy per generated token lies far from the days before them, next to the changes of version, driver, model file or configuration around them. Periods can be dates, RFC 3339 times or amounts of time ago such as 24h or 7d.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens report [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--by` | Group by none, hour or day | `none` |
| `--esg` | Report the environment of the node: Scope 2 emissions, cost, water and SCI, by backend and model |  |
| `--from` | Start of the period | `24h` |
| `--group` | Report by backend, model or consumer instead of by domain |  |
| `--html` | Write the report as a printable page to this file |  |
| `--regressions` | List the days whose energy per generated token is a regression or an improvement, and the changes of context |  |
| `--to` | End of the period | `now` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens report
greenlens report --from 7d --by day
greenlens report --from 7d --group model
greenlens report --from 30d --regressions
greenlens report --from 2026-10-01 --to 2026-11-01 --esg --html report.html
greenlens report --from 2026-10-01 --to 2026-11-01 --output csv
```

## greenlens restore

Check a backup made by 'greenlens backup' and replace the database with it. The agent must be stopped. The current database is first copied next to it, unless --no-keep is given, and a backup from an older version is updated to the current schema.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens restore <file> [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--database` | Replace this database file instead of the one of the configuration |  |
| `--no-keep` | Do not keep a copy of the current database |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens restore greenlens-2026-10-20.db
sudo -u greenlens greenlens restore --database /var/lib/greenlens/greenlens.db /srv/backups/greenlens.db
```

## greenlens sci

Compute the Software Carbon Intensity of ISO/IEC 21031 for a period: the operational emissions of the energy, hour by hour, plus the embodied carbon of the server and the GPU, per functional unit. With --group, also for each backend, model or consumer, which carry the share of the hardware that their energy is of the energy of the node. The unit comes from indicators.sci.functional_unit unless --unit names another.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens sci [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--from` | Start of the period | `24h` |
| `--group` | Also report each backend, model or consumer |  |
| `--html` | Write the report as a printable page to this file |  |
| `--to` | End of the period | `now` |
| `--unit` | Functional unit: 1k_generated_tokens, request or consumer |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens sci --from 30d
greenlens sci --from 7d --group model
greenlens sci --from 2026-10-01 --to 2026-11-01 --unit request --output csv
```

## greenlens setup-permissions

Show the changes that give the greenlens-power group read access to the RAPL energy counters, and optionally the IPMI device and the CAP_PERFMON capability for perf_event. Nothing changes until the command runs as root with --apply.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens setup-permissions [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--apply` | Apply the plan; needs root |  |
| `--ipmi` | Also give the group access to the IPMI device |  |
| `--perfmon` | Also grant CAP_PERFMON to this binary, for perf_event |  |
| `--user` | Add this user to the group |  |
| `--yes` | Do not ask for confirmation |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens setup-permissions
sudo greenlens setup-permissions --apply --user $USER
sudo greenlens setup-permissions --apply --perfmon --ipmi
```

## greenlens token

Create, list and revoke the access tokens that programs and remote browsers use with the HTTP API. Each token has a role: viewer reads measurements, operator also runs benchmarks and calibrations, admin also manages tokens and backups. Tokens are kept as argon2id hashes; the secret is shown only when it is created. With the agent running, the changes go through it and its audit log; otherwise the token file is changed directly.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens token [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|

## greenlens token create

Create an access token with a name, a role and an optional expiry, and print its secret once.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens token create [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--expires` | Lifetime of the token, such as 90d, 12w or 36h, or never | `never` |
| `--name` | Name of the token, such as grafana or ci |  |
| `--role` | Role of the token: viewer, operator or admin | `viewer` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens token create --name grafana --role viewer --expires 90d
sudo -u greenlens greenlens token create --name admin --role admin
```

## greenlens token list

List the access tokens with their role, creation time and expiry. Secrets are never shown.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens token list [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens token list
greenlens token list --output json
```

## greenlens token revoke

Revoke the access token with the given id or name. Programs using it are refused from then on.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens token revoke <token> [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens token revoke grafana
greenlens token revoke 3f9a1c0b7d2e
```

## greenlens top

Open a live view of the agent in the terminal: the power of every domain, the backends and models with their energy per token, the consumers and the energy sources. Keys 1 to 4 or Tab change the view, / filters, s sorts, p pauses, e exports the view to CSV, ? shows the help of the view and q quits. It works over SSH from 80 by 24 characters, in ASCII when the locale is not UTF-8 and without color with --no-color or NO_COLOR.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens top [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--ascii` | Draw with ASCII only, for terminals without Unicode |  |
| `--refresh` | How often the agent is read, from 250ms to 1m | `1s` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens top
greenlens top --refresh 5s --ascii
```
